transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-15
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Mark Rivera (CISO, Montara), Sara Kim (Director IT Ops, Montara), David Chen (SRE, Montara)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, this is Priya our solutions engineer. quick agenda — go over SOC2/ISO, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, encryption/KMS questions, then deep dive on incident response / BCDR (RTO/RPO) and the escalation path.
[00:22] Mark: Thanks, Jordan. Main concern is we need clear RTO/RPO numbers and an escalation matrix. We also want BYOK and HSM support for keys.
[00:30] Priya: Yep makes sense. I'll outline how our architecture handles keys and incident processes. quick caveat: some product names might sound off in the transcript, e.g., Redwood Dedecated — that's our Dedicated reserved capacity offering.
[00:48] Sara: On logs, we need 1 year min of audit log retention and ability to stream to Splunk. Also SOC2 evidence and ISO control mappings for our auditors.
[01:05] Jordan: We can share SOC2 Type II and the ISO mapping doc. retention defaults are 90 days in hosted but we offer longer retention as an add-on or through export to customer SIEM.
[01:25] David: For production LLM endpoints, what's your SLA for uptime and how do credits work if you miss SLOs?
[01:35] Jordan: Our Dedicated offering has an SLA with 99.95% uptime target for critical endpoints; hosted tier is typically 99.9 depending on contract. Credits are pro-rata and we provide SLA terms in the contract. we'll follow up with the SLA PDF.
[01:52] Mark: RTO is key. For us, recovery time objective target is 60 minutes for customer-facing inference services, and RPO ideally 5 minutes. Can you support that?
[02:10] Priya: short answer: yes for Dedicated in most cases. we have cross-region failover, automatic KV cache resyncs, and warm standby pools. realistic RTO depends on model size, kv cache warmup, and whether you want automatic failover or manual promotion. For a 60 min RTO and 5 min RPO we recommend warm standby with KV cache snapshotting and prefix cache prewarm steps — we can run a tabletop to validate.
[02:40] Sara: what about data residency during failover? if traffic moves regionally due to a failover that could break compliance.
[02:50] Priya: good point. we support routing policies that stick to allowed regions. for Dedicated / Private deployments you can constrain failover to a set of approved regions. if you need strict on-prem, we have Private deployments and air-gapped options.
[03:10] Mark: encryption — at rest and in transit? KMS specifics?
[03:18] Jordan: encryption in transit is TLS 1.2/1.3, at rest we use envelope encryption backed by cloud KMS for hosted; Dedicated and Private support customer-managed keys (BYOK) and HSM integrations. Priya can share the HSM/KMS checklist.
[03:35] Priya: yes BYOK flow: customer provides key (AWS KMS or external HSM), we use envelope keys per-tenant, rotate per policy, and you can configure key rotation windows. there are some operational caveats around emergency key rotation during incident — we'll document.
[03:55] David: how do you handle access control and RBAC? we need role separation: admins, operators, developers, auditors.
[04:04] Priya: RBAC supports granular roles. default roles: admin, deployer, viewer; you can add custom roles. SSO via SAML/Okta/AzureAD supported; we can push SCIM for user provisioning. audit logs capture user actions and API calls.
[04:25] Sara: audit log format? do you provide a raw event stream we can ingest?
[04:30] Priya: yes, audit events are JSON lines, include request id, user id, action, resource, timestamp. retention configurable; default 90 days, add-on for 365+ or push to SIEM (Splunk, Datadog, ArcSight). we'll include example log schema.
[04:50] Mark: incident lifecycle — what does your escalation look like for Sev1 vs Sev2? we need primary/secondary contacts and an SLA to commit to response times.
[05:00] Jordan: Our standard escalation: automated monitoring triggers incident ticketing and paging. For Sev1 we have a 15-minute initial response target (acknowledge) by oncall infra; engineering bridge within 30 minutes; active remediation with updates every 15 minutes until mitigation. For Dedicated customers we can tighten these numbers in contract.
[05:24] Priya: add to that: we create a major-incident bridge (Zoom/Teams) with Redwood oncall, assigned SE, and optionally a designated customer liaison. Post-incident we do RCA and provide a report within 5 business days for critical incidents; full root-cause and mitigation plan within 10 business days. that is our typical cadence.
[05:50] David: what about runbooks and playbooks? do you provide examples or do we write our own?
[05:56] Priya: we provide template runbooks for common failure modes (model OOM, KV cache corruption, provisioning failure, network partition). we'll share the templates and can co-author them during the tabletop.
[06:12] Mark: escalation policy — who gets paged in Redwood org? do you have a single phone number or an escalation chain?
[06:20] Jordan: we provide an escalation matrix: first-level oncall (SRE), second-level infra eng, third-level platform eng lead, plus the assigned AE/SE. We'll put that in the runbook. You can nominate who should be paged at which severity.
[06:40] Sara: in the event of a region outage, do you perform automatic failover? how do you ensure RPO 5 min?
[06:48] Priya: automatic failover is an option but for strict compliance customers we recommend controlled failover — we maintain replication of session state and KV snapshots, those can be written to a cross-region durable store every X minutes. achieving 5 min RPO usually requires continuous replication with small snapshot windows and some caching tradeoffs. we'll need to run tests against your model and token patterns.
[07:15] Mark: ok, we want to run a POC that verifies RTO/RPO with our critical model. can Redwood instrument cold start times and KV cache warmup?
[07:25] Priya: yes, we can run a benchmark harness — capture cold-start, warm-start, per-token latency distributions. we'll include instrumentation hooks and can provide custom scripts.
[07:40] Jordan: on the legal side, we'll also share the data processing addendum, details on retention, and data residency options — for Private deployments it's customer controlled.
[07:52] David: if we have an incident where keys are suspected compromised, what's the rotation / emergency key revocation flow?
[08:00] Priya: emergency key rotation: customer triggers rotation or Redwood can rotate under pre-agreed protocol; we use envelope keys so we can re-encrypt without needing to re-materialize model weights. HSM-backed BYOK might require planned windows. we'll document the step-by-step and SLA for emergency key rotation.
[08:24] Mark: audit — auditors will want chain-of-custody and timeline of actions. can you provide immutable logs and signed timestamps?
[08:33] Jordan: audit logs are append-only and we can provide signed log exports for the period. for Dedicated you can also ship logs to your SIEM for retention and chain-of-custody.
[08:50] Sara: are there any single points of failure in your control plane for Dedicated?
[08:56] Priya: control plane is multi-AZ, redundant, with failover. data plane is where models run; for Dedicated we offer replicated pools. Private deployments remove Redwood control plane dependency. we'll include an architecture diagram in the follow-up.
[09:18] Mark: SLA credits specifics? how much credit for 99.95 vs 99.9?
[09:24] Jordan: typical schedule: if uptime < promised threshold you receive monthly service credits pro-rata — e.g., below 99.95% could be 10% credit, lower bands increase. exact numbers in contract. we'll provide the table.
[09:40] David: do you provide war rooms and designated escalation contacts during an incident for enterprise customers?
[09:46] Jordan: yes enterprise customers get a named technical account manager and dedicated escalation path; we run war room support during Sev1 incidents.
[09:55] Priya: also worth noting for BCDR: we recommend periodic drills (quarterly or semi-annual) and we'll co-run them. those drills validate RTO/RPO, failover, and runbook steps.
[10:10] Mark: ok that sounds good. can you confirm the timeline for the artifacts? SOC2 by Tue (3/17), SSO guide by 3/18, SLA by 3/19?
[10:20] Jordan: yes we'll aim for that. Priya will take the technical docs.
[10:26] Sara: one more question — during failover will API tokens be invalidated? what's session continuity?
[10:33] Priya: tokens are valid unless you rotate them; session continuity depends on prefix caching; when we failover we replay prefix cache where possible but some sessions may need rehydration. for low RTO we recommend sticky routing and warm standby to minimize rehydration.
[10:54] Mark: can we get a sample incident playbook for a model OOM and for a regional network partition?
[11:00] Priya: yes, will share both.
[11:08] Jordan: let's recap next steps — we'll share SOC2/ISO artifacts, SSO/SAML guide, RBAC matrix, KMS/BYOK checklist, SLA PDF, and schedule tabletop drill. sara will confirm participants. any other items?
[11:25] Mark: please include contact for escalation (pager/email/phone) and the nightly oncall rotation.
[11:32] Jordan: noted, we'll provide the escalation matrix and sample oncall rota.
[11:40] Sara: thanks, this was productive.
[11:43] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up in email and share the docs.
[11:50] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: minor transcription errors, occasional speaker mislabels and product name typos (e.g., 'Redwood Dedecated').
